definition: Linear Programming Boosting (LPBoost) is a supervised classifier from the boosting family of classifiers.
details: LPBoost maximizes a margin between training samples of different classes, and thus also belongs to the class of margin classifier algorithms. Consider a classification function f : X → { − 1 , 1 } , {\displaystyle f:{\mathcal {X}}\to \{-1,1\},} which classifies samples from a space X {\displaystyle {\mathcal {X}}} into one of two classes, labelled 1 and -1, respectively. LPBoost is an algorithm for learning such a classification function, given a set of training examples with known class labels. LPBoost is a machine learning technique especially suited for joint classification and feature selection in structured domains.

explainer.lead: LPBoost is a boosting classifier that maximizes the margin between classes using linear programming. It belongs to the margin-classifier family alongside other boosting methods.

tiers.eli5: It's like combining many weak guessers and adjusting how much you trust each one so the final vote leaves the widest possible gap between the two answers.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it when a margin-based ensemble with a linear-programming formulation fits the problem. A pitfall is that the LP formulation can be slow or sensitive at scale compared with simpler boosting variants.
tiers.paperLevel: LPBoost learns a classification function f: X -> {-1,1} from labeled training examples by maximizing the margin between training samples of different classes; it is a supervised boosting classifier and a margin classifier.

explainer.example: Given labeled examples of two classes, LPBoost learns weights over weak learners that maximize the margin separating the classes.
